newsitem.title: CHINA: Earthquake rocks northwest China, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake rocks northwest China, no casualties.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.3 on the Richter scale jolted a county in China's northwestern Xinjiang region on Wednesday, but there were no immediate reports of casualties, local officials said.
The earthquake struck at 4.20 a.m. (2040 GMT Tuesday) in Jiashi county, where up to 50 people were killed in an earthquake last month, the official Xinhua news agency said.
"People were asleep at the time, but some residents fled their homes after the earthquake," said one local official reached by telephone.

An earthquake of 6.4 magnitude caused widespread damage and killed up to 50 people in Jiashi on January 21, and the area populated mainly by sheep herders and cotton farmers has since been rocked by hundreds of aftershocks.
"Many people are still sleeping outside because there have been so many aftershocks," the official said.
At least three aftershocks rocked Jiashi on Monday, and the tremors have been an almost daily occurrence since the first major earthquake on January 21, he said.
More aftershocks were expected, he said.
